title: Threshing Floor and Donkeys
preview: Back outside, the stone circle tells the story of wheat before milling. Here, harvest, animal strength and patient hands prepared grain for the windmill.
details: The threshing floor was an essential outdoor workspace. Wheat and other crops were spread across the stone circle, then pressed and broken so the useful grain could be separated.
In the past, a donkey walked around the center post, helping loosen the harvested crop. Afterward, people continued the work by separating and cleaning the wheat.
This stop makes the windmill story fuller. Flour did not begin inside the mill; it began with fields, weather, harvesters, animals and the repeated work of many hands.
Mylotopi also keeps the memory of village animals close to the visitor experience. Please admire them calmly and from a respectful distance.
Continue toward the Italian tunnel and cellar, where the atmosphere changes from open rural work to cool stone and wartime memory.

items.text: Follow the circle with your eyes.
